already-have.reason: Not implemented and not refuted. No board/hardware field exists in either manifest format or in any update-path check, and the proposal is the already-banked issue #487 whose stated precondition ("when a second board/revision is introduced") is now met in-tree (BOARD=iota2|pq1). It does not contradict a recorded decision, but it is over-prioritised and two parts of it collide with recorded constraints. (1) The V6 preimage is frozen at 121 bytes under Draft 1.1; any field addition needs an approved spec digest, dual review and an owner stage decision (CLAUDE.md; tracked by #543/#545/#540). (2) Draft 1.1 section 6.4 already defines the product namespace as exactly (PQFW_V6, embedded vendor-key fingerprint) and says "no unsigned product string creates a sub-namespace" and that another product needs "a new manifest schema/domain or dedicated key" — so the proposal's interim unsigned V1 fast-reject cuts against that text, and a per-board key or domain is the spec-native alternative the proposal does not consider. P0 is not supported: iota2 is the ST dev kit (bench only) and pq1 is the sole production board, nothing has shipped, `make release` is a hard refusal, and the whole V1 update path is legacy bench-only. The cross-board hazard is real on the bench (PA8 = SE rail enable on pq1 vs button on iota2) but there is no shipping exposure today.

Corrections to the proposal itself:
- "The V6 draft ... was frozen without one" understates it: section 6.4 (docs/security/a-b-firmware-rollback-architecture.md:2430-2441) deliberately makes (domain, vendor key) the only product namespace. The proposal must be framed as an owner spec amendment choosing between (a) signed hw_model/hw_revision fields (121 -> 127 B, new digest, new schema byte) and (b) per-board domain tag or dedicated vendor key, which needs no preimage change. Option (b) has a cost: section 6.4 says a different domain under a shared key is still counted by the global C10 signing budget.
- The interim "unsigned fast-reject on V1 + make release refusal" is weak. `make release` already refuses unconditionally (Makefile:2913-2914). An unsigned V1 field is attacker-editable, and adding it to the 0x02 layout changes a legacy bench format slated for replacement. The useful interim piece is narrower: a build/packaging-side check that the board feature of the ELF matches the intended target.
- Adjacent observation, not verified beyond the two lines: BOARD defaults to iota2 (Makefile:43) and RELEASE_FEATURES takes $(BOARD_FEATURE) (Makefile:2662), so a restored release pipeline would build the dev-kit pin map unless BOARD=pq1 is passed. I found no issue for this in a title search.
- Kind is mixed (owner spec decision + firmware + fwsign/release tooling), not pure firmware. Cost M is plausible only after the spec gate; the gate dominates.
- The FSBL-side check adds bytes and boot time to the component that the A/B rollback review flagged as the NO-GO budget; a compare-before-C10 is tiny but must be counted against the FSBL geometry (#540).

feasible.reason:
The gap is real and the proposal closes it, but P0 is inflated, the threat is overstated, and two design details conflict with the code.

Premise checks out: neither the V1 preimage (fw_version + two hashes) nor the 121-byte V6 preimage carries a board field. A grep for hw_model / hw_revision / board_id across fw-manifest, fsbl, secure/src/fw_update, cmd_fw_* and fwsign returns nothing. Issue #487 is open and labelled priority:low, with the explicit trigger "when a second board exists"; that trigger has fired. A signed model tag compared against a compiled-in constant does stop a validly signed wrong-board image. I could not construct a bypass of a signed field short of the existing signature-forgery or fault-injection residuals. The unsigned V1 interim check is trivially bypassed by an attacker who edits the tag; the proposal already calls it non-authoritative, so it only catches accidents.

Feasible on pq1 with no board change. A few constant bytes and one compare fit the FSBL (28,704 B LOAD span against 32 KiB) and the secure image. Kind stays firmware.

Why P0 is not honest:
- An attacker cannot mint a signed wrong-board image. The threat needs the vendor to sign an iota2 build with the production key that pq1 units trust.
- `make release` is a hard refusal today, the S-2 fence blocks every mode-production build, and iota2 is a dev kit.
- The consequence is availability, not key compromise. An iota2 image on pq1 configures PA8 as a pulled-up button input, so the SE rail is never enabled; unlock fails, and since FW_* needs a PIN unlock the device cannot be updated back. That is a brick at RDP-2, not "physically dangerous" in the secrets sense.
- The real driver for doing it before ship is the FSBL freeze: the FSBL-side check cannot be added after RDP-2 + WRP, and future pq1 revisions will need it. That makes it P1.
feasible.corrections:
1. Threat wording. Replace "physically dangerous" with: availability brick, plus a pin-ownership regression. An iota2 image on pq1 leaves LDO2_EN (PA8) as a pulled-up input, so the secure elements are unpowered or indeterminate. It also hands PA15/PB5/PB15 to the non-secure world as USB pins, which on pq1 are SE_RST / SE1_EN / LCM_EN, and drives PA9 as USART1 TX onto pq1's USB_FS_VBUS sense net. No secret is disclosed. The attacker precondition is a vendor-signed wrong-board image under the same vendor key, i.e. a release-process error, not an attacker capability.

2. "Reject BEFORE the expensive C10 verify" contradicts secure-world design. `verify_manifest` deliberately does not short-circuit (timing normalization, finding C). The board check must be folded into that all-steps-run chain, not placed as an early return. In the FSBL `filter_valid` it must use `fi::check_true_into_sentinel` + `scrub_sentinel_register` (F15 discipline), not a bare `?`. Otherwise it is a single-instruction-skip gate.

3. V6 is not wired into any consumer. `fw-manifest/src/v6.rs` exists, but fsbl, secure and fwsign never reference it. The proposed edits to `verify_manifest` / `filter_valid` therefore act on V1 only. The V6 part is purely a spec amendment (121 -> 127 B, new digest), gated by dual review + owner stage decision. That governance is the real cost driver.

4. Two cheaper authenticated alternatives the proposal misses, neither needing a preimage change:
   - Per-board vendor keys. `vendor_fpr` is already inside the signed V6 preimage and is checked in V1; `fsbl/build.rs` has no board-specific key handling today, so the same FSBL_VENDOR_PUBKEY (and the dev fixture key) is accepted by both boards.
   - A board tag in an allocated section of the secure image. It is covered by the signed `secure_hash`, and the FSBL `verify_images` hashes the full secure_len span, so the tag is authenticated transitively. Trade-off: it can only reject after the image is written and hashed, so the BEGIN-time check still needs a manifest field or a companion-supplied pre-check.

5. Bench exposure is live today, unlike production. All bench builds share the dev fixture key, so a cross-board .pqfw is accepted now. An unsigned/accident-grade check has real bench value independent of V6.

6. The FSBL-side check is only load-bearing pre-RDP-2 or for images that bypass the secure world. At RDP-2 the only install path is CMD_FW_*, so the secure-world check is the primary gate and the FSBL check is defence in depth. But it must exist in the FSBL before WRP + RDP-2 freeze, because it can never be added later. State this as the scheduling reason.

7. Trezor citation errors:
   - `image.c:140-166` and `boot_header.c:183-186` are correct.
   - `boardloader/main.c:119-130` is `fih_delay` / `fih_ensure`; `board_capabilities_t capabilities` begins at 131-134.
   - `wf_firmware_update.c:131-135` is `version_compare`, not a model check. The model checks are at :105 (current header), :150 (`check_vendor_header_model`) and :170 (`check_image_model`).
   - The board_capabilities consumer is `core/embed/sec/image/stm32/boot_image.c:119,137,163-175`.
   - Trezor's `hw_revision` is an exact match (`!=`), so the proposal's "range rule" has no Trezor precedent.
   - The risk note that Trezor "shipped expiry without enforcing it" is wrong. `expiry` is repurposed as a compatibility-break bit (`(expiry & 1) == 0` is rejected on non-TT models), with a T2T1 carve-out that accepts hw_model == 0.
   - The check is compiled out under TREZOR_EMULATOR.
   - Issue #487 itself cites `header_pq.c`, not the files the proposal lists.

8. Cost. S for the in-image tag / per-board-key route plus the fwsign `--hw-model` and release-gate cross-check. M for the V6 preimage amendment (governance, new digest, re-pinned tests). Overall M stands.
